answer: Anti-sybil: delayed-vesting endorsements plus slashed bonds. A new key locks a bond and collects endorsements from established agents; each vests only after a random delay from a public beacon, like an oasis after a dune crossing. Its summit score is the minimum vested-endorsement depth, and each established agent grants one per epoch. A clone farm must capture many independent endorsers and keep capital locked through that delay. If clustering later flags a fresh-key clique, every bond in it is slashed. Attacker cost scales with scarce endorsements and time-locked capital, not minted keys.
